title: Recorder offers NumpadEnter and NumpadEqual, but they register Enter and the letter E system-wide
claim: KEYS (Hotkeys.tsx:83) accepts "NumpadEnter" and "NumpadEqual", and KEY_LABELS shows them as "Num Enter" / "Num =". parse_key accepts both (hotkey.rs:315-316: `"NUMPADENTER" | "NUMENTER" => Ok(NumpadEnter)`, `"NUMPADEQUAL" | "NUMEQUAL" => Ok(NumpadEqual)`). key_to_vk then maps `Code::NumpadEnter => VK_RETURN` and `Code::NumpadEqual => VK_E` (windows/mod.rs:308-309), and register() passes that VK to RegisterHotKey. Windows reports both Enter keys as VK_RETURN, so "NumpadEnter" takes the main Enter key as well. "NumpadEqual" takes the E key. risky() returns false whenever a modifier is present (Hotkeys.tsx:138), so no warning appears. apply_hotkeys checks for duplicates by string (`one.eq_ignore_ascii_case(other)`, commands.rs:211), so "Ctrl+Enter" on one action and "Ctrl+NumpadEnter" on another both pass. The second RegisterHotKey then fails with ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED, and the user is told "Ctrl+NumpadEnter is already taken by another program." (lib.rs:827-829). The clash is with ClippiBoy's own other action.
scenario: A user binds Save clip to Ctrl+NumpadEnter, displayed as "Ctrl + Num Enter". From then on Ctrl+Enter in every program saves a clip and never reaches the program: send in Slack, Teams and Discord, send mail in Outlook, submit in web forms. Shift+NumpadEnter steals Shift+Enter in the same way, which is the newline key in chat apps. On a keyboard with a numpad '=' key, a bare 'NumpadEqual' binding swallows every 'e' typed system-wide, and 'Ctrl+NumpadEqual' takes Ctrl+E.
fix: Remove "NumpadEqual" from KEYS: global-hotkey 0.8.0 maps it to VK_E and there is no correct mapping. Either drop "NumpadEnter" too, or record it as "Enter" with the label "Enter", because RegisterHotKey cannot tell the two Enter keys apart. In apply_hotkeys, compare the parsed shortcuts after mapping them to their VK instead of comparing strings, and report an internal clash as "used twice", not "taken by another program".

title: risky() treats any modifier, Shift included, as safe: Shift+letter, Shift+Enter and Ctrl+C get no warning
claim: risky() is the only guard against bindings that interfere with typing. It returns false as soon as any part is in MODIFIERS: `if (keys.some((key) => MODIFIERS.includes(key))) return false;` (line 138). MODIFIERS includes "Shift" (line 125). So "Shift+S", "Shift+1", "Shift+Space", "Shift+Enter" and "Shift+Tab" produce no warning, although each one types a character or performs a text-field action. The same holds for Ctrl+C/V/X/Z/A and Alt+F4. The core registers every one of them with RegisterHotKey (windows/mod.rs:95-96), which is system-wide and takes the keystroke away from the foreground app. The warning at lines 259-264 only covers bare keys.
scenario: A user sees the warning on a bare 'S' and switches to Shift+S, expecting that adding a modifier makes it safe. No warning appears. From then on every capital S typed in any program (chat, Word, a password field) saves a clip, and the letter never appears. Binding Ctrl+C or Ctrl+V likewise breaks copy and paste in every application, again without a warning.
fix: Treat Shift-only combinations with a printable or editing key as risky, and do the same for Ctrl+Alt+<printable> (see the AltGr finding). Also warn for well-known editing and system chords: Ctrl+A/C/V/X/Z/Y, Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter, Alt+F4, Alt+Space and Alt+Tab. For example, take mods = keys.slice(0, -1) and key = keys.at(-1); return !HARMLESS.test(key) when mods is ['Shift'], or when it contains both Ctrl and Alt; then check a small deny-list.

title: Recorder stores the physical event.code but Windows matches the layout VK, so non-US layouts bind a different key than the one pressed
claim: accelerator() stores event.code (line 109). event.code names a physical key by its position on a US-QWERTY board. parse_key turns it into the Code of the same name. key_to_vk then maps that Code to the VK the key has on a US layout: Backquote=>VK_OEM_3, Semicolon=>VK_OEM_1, BracketLeft=>VK_OEM_4, Minus=>VK_OEM_MINUS, Slash=>VK_OEM_2, KeyY=>VK_Y, KeyZ=>VK_Z (mod.rs:230-252). RegisterHotKey matches virtual keys, and Windows assigns those from the active layout. On any layout where a key's VK differs from the US one, the hotkey fires on a different physical key from the one pressed. German QWERTZ (kbdgr): ^ (code Backquote) registers VK_OEM_3, which is the Ö key. ß (Minus) registers the '-' key, ´ (Equal) the '+' key, Ü (BracketLeft) the ß key, + (BracketRight) the ´ key, Ö (Semicolon) the Ü key, # (Backslash) the ^ key and '-' (Slash) the # key. The key labelled Z (KeyY) registers the key labelled Y, and the reverse. Only Ä (Quote), comma and period line up. UK (kbduk): ` (Backquote) registers VK_OEM_3, which is the apostrophe key, and ' (Quote) registers VK_OEM_7, which is the # key. keyLabel() prints the US code name ("Backquote", "Semicolon", "Y"). That is neither what is printed on the pressed key nor recognisably the key that was actually bound. Because the VK is resolved at key-press time, switching input language (Win+Space) also moves every punctuation hotkey.
scenario: A German user sets 'Console over the game' to ^, the usual game-console key left of 1. It is stored as "Backquote" and registered as VK_OEM_3. Pressing ^ does nothing. Every ö typed in any program opens the console and the letter is swallowed. The bare-key warning does appear, but the user reads it as being about ^. On a UK layout the same binding makes every apostrophe typed open the console. A German user who presses Alt+Z in the recorder sees and gets Alt+Y.
fix: Record what Windows will actually match. In WebView2 on Windows, event.keyCode is the virtual key for the active layout. Map it back to the global-hotkey name whose key_to_vk yields that VK (220 -> "Backslash", 192 -> "Backquote", 90 -> "Z" and so on), and take the label from event.key or navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap(). The alternative is in Rust: convert the code to its scan code, resolve it with MapVirtualKeyExW(MAPVK_VSC_TO_VK_EX) against the current layout, and register that VK.

title: AltGr is recorded as Ctrl+Alt, and any Ctrl+Alt hotkey swallows the AltGr character on that key (@, {, \, €, Polish letters)
claim: On Windows the AltGr key is delivered as LCtrl+RAlt, and Chromium/WebView2 reports AltGr keystrokes with ctrlKey and altKey both true. accelerator() builds the modifiers from ctrlKey and altKey only (lines 104-105) and never checks getModifierState("AltGraph"), so AltGr+Q is stored as "Ctrl+Alt+Q". register() turns that into MOD_CONTROL|MOD_ALT plus VK_Q. Windows hotkey matching sees Ctrl and Alt both down while AltGr is held, so the hotkey fires whenever the user types the AltGr character on that key, and the character is consumed. risky() does not warn because the binding has modifiers (line 138).
scenario: A German user binds Screenshot to Ctrl+Alt+Q, or presses AltGr+Q in the recorder, which stores the same thing. From then on '@' cannot be typed in any program: AltGr+Q takes a screenshot instead, which breaks email addresses and @-mentions. The same happens with Ctrl+Alt+E (€), Ctrl+Alt+7/8/9/0 ({ [ ] }) and Ctrl+Alt+Minus (\). On Polish Programmer, Ctrl+Alt+A/C/E/L/N/O/S/X/Z swallow ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż.
fix: In accelerator(), ignore keystrokes with event.getModifierState("AltGraph") set, or tell the user that AltGr cannot be used. In risky(), warn for Ctrl+Alt+<printable key>, at least when navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap() or event.key shows that the key produces a character with AltGr on the current layout.

title: Hotkeys that fail to register at startup fail silently, and one such key then blocks every change to the other four
claim: At startup the error from register_hotkeys only goes to the log: `if let Err(err) = register_hotkeys(handle) { log::warn!("{err}"); }` (lib.rs:1265-1267). resume_hotkeys also only logs (commands.rs:257-258). The config keeps the combination, and the Hotkeys page has no per-row status, so it shows the key as bound. register_hotkeys returns a single error that lists every failed combination (lib.rs:823-831). apply_hotkeys treats any failure as fatal for the whole set: it rolls back all five values and re-registers the old ones (commands.rs:228-237). It does not check whether the failed combination is one the user just changed. So a combination the user never touched, but that cannot be registered, makes every later edit of any other row fail and revert.
scenario: The save-clip combination is held by another tool that starts earlier at logon. Another way to get here: the user follows the hint at Hotkeys.tsx:262 ('F keys and PrtSc are the quieter spots') and binds PrtSc on Windows 11 with 'Use the Print screen key to open screen capture' on, where the key likely belongs to the system. On every start registration fails without any message, and the settings page shows the key as set although it does nothing. The user then tries to move Screenshot to F9: set_hotkeys returns "Ctrl+Shift+S is already taken by another program." and F9 is reverted, although F9 is free. Unbinding a different action fails the same way. Only changing the one broken row, which the user had no reason to suspect, gets them unstuck.
fix: Have register_hotkeys return a result per action. In apply_hotkeys, reject and roll back only the actions whose value changed and failed. Keep unchanged actions that fail to register, and flag them instead. Show startup failures to the user, either with notify() or with a hotkey-status query that the Hotkeys page renders next to each row.

title: Default hotkeys take over some of the most common app shortcuts system-wide (Ctrl+Shift+P/R/B/S)
claim: The defaults are "Ctrl+Shift+S" (save), "Ctrl+Shift+B" (buffer), "Ctrl+Shift+P" (screenshot), "Ctrl+Shift+R" (record) and "Alt+C" (console). All of them parse, and register_hotkeys registers them with RegisterHotKey at every start. RegisterHotKey is system-wide and exclusive: the keystroke goes to ClippiBoy's hidden window and never reaches the foreground app. These chords are standard shortcuts elsewhere. Ctrl+Shift+R is hard reload in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Ctrl+Shift+P is the VS Code command palette and Firefox's private window. Ctrl+Shift+B is the bookmarks bar in Chrome and Edge and Build in VS Code and Visual Studio. Ctrl+Shift+S is Save As in VS Code, Photoshop, GIMP and Blender. toggle_recording_and_notify starts a recording regardless of whether a game is running (lib.rs:199-207). risky() never flags these because they have modifiers.
scenario: After a default install, with the app running in the tray, a developer presses Ctrl+Shift+P in VS Code. The command palette does not open; a screenshot is taken instead. A user presses Ctrl+Shift+R to hard-reload a web page, and a screen recording starts with a banner and a sound. Ctrl+Shift+B in Chrome toggles the replay buffer instead of the bookmarks bar. Nothing tells the user that these shortcuts have been taken away from their other apps.
fix: Choose defaults that rarely collide, for example Alt+F9/Alt+F10-style keys or Ctrl+Alt+<F-key> as other recorders use, or leave record and screenshot unbound by default. Say during setup that the hotkeys apply in every program.

title: Recovered recordings are indexed only after every leftover is finished; a quit during a later one orphans the earlier MP4s for good
claim: lib.rs:279 `let clips = state.recover_recordings(...)` returns only after the loop at state.rs:1152-1170 has finalized every leftover. Only then does lib.rs:283-294 call `library.insert`, `store_tags`, emit `clip-saved` and show the toast. Each successful `recorder::finalize` has already deleted its work folder (`std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir)`, recorder.rs:604) before it returns. So from the moment leftover N is finalized until the insert loop runs, recording N exists only as an MP4 on disk: no work folder and no library row. Finalizing leftover N+1 takes minutes for a long recording (ffprobe counts the whole stream, then sum_tracks, then an AAC encode of every track), and a tray Quit (tray.rs:139-148 calls app.exit(0) without waiting), an update install, a crash or a Windows shutdown in that time kills the thread. On the next start leftovers() no longer sees N because its meta.json is gone, and nothing scans the clip folder: the only read_dir callers are tools.rs:295, recorder.rs:617, commands.rs:1271 and edit.rs:161. N's MP4 therefore never reaches the library, and its stems (stems::dir(id)) and thumbnail are orphaned too.
scenario: Two leftovers exist: recording A was abandoned (tray Quit mid-recording, by design 'finished on the next start'), its recovery the next session failed or was cut short, and recording B was then abandoned too. On the next start A is muxed into <Game>/Recordings/..._rec_....mp4 and .recording/A is deleted. While B's multi-minute finalize runs, the user quits from the tray or Windows restarts. A's hour-long recording stays on disk but never appears in the gallery or the Recordings tab, on this start or any later one, and no toast ever said it was finished.
fix: Insert each recovered clip (row, tags, clip-saved, toast) as soon as its finalize returns, for example with a per-clip callback passed into recover_recordings instead of a Vec returned at the end. Better still, write the row, or a marker naming the output path in meta.json, before deleting the work folder, so a kill at any point leaves something the next start can reconcile.

title: Leftover recordings are looked for only in the current clip folder; after a folder change they are never finished or mentioned
claim: recover_recordings takes `let clip_dir = self.config_snapshot().clip_dir;` (state.rs:1149) and scans only `<that>/.recording` (recorder.rs:617). A work folder is created under whatever clip folder was configured when its recording started (recorder.rs:139). set_clip_dir (commands.rs:267-290) does not refuse a change while a recording runs, and it does not look for, move or finish leftovers in the old folder. Nothing remembers earlier clip folders for recovery: allow_existing_clip_dirs only grants them to the asset protocol. A leftover in an earlier clip folder is therefore never recovered.
scenario: (a) While recording onto C:, the 'Clip drive filling up' banner (lib.rs:913-924) prompts the user to switch the clip folder to D: under Settings > Storage. The recording keeps writing to C:\...\ClippiBoy\.recording\<id>. The user then quits from the tray (abandon_recording) or the PC crashes. On the next start recovery scans D:\...\.recording and finds nothing. (b) A recovery fails for lack of room (VP-13), and the user moves the clip folder to a bigger drive to fix it. The failed leftover is never retried. Either way the recording stays on the old drive as gigabytes of raw H.264 and PCM, never muxed, never shown and still taking the space, and the user is never told.
fix: Recover from every clip folder that may hold leftovers: the current one, the previous config value, and the parent folders of clips in the library. Alternatively, record each work folder's path in the data dir when it is created. At minimum, check the old folder in set_clip_dir and finish its leftovers or tell the user.

title: Failed recoveries are silent and repeated in full on every start, and unrecoverable leftovers are never cleared
claim: Both failure branches of recover_recordings only `log::warn!`: 'left alone' (state.rs:1159) and 'not finished' (state.rs:1168). lib.rs:279-294 handles only the successes it gets back. There is no toast, banner or sound, no attempt counter, no backoff and no way to discard. The folder is kept on purpose (recorder.rs:552-555, 'the next start tries again'), so the whole job runs again at every launch. For a crashed recording, count_frames makes ffprobe read the entire H.264 stream (recorder.rs:540, 501-520); then sum_tracks rewrites all of mix.pcm and every track is AAC-encoded, only to fail the same way again. When autostarted this happens at Windows sign-in, while the user is starting a game. Some leftovers can never succeed: a crash before the video writer's first 1 MiB BufWriter flush (recorder.rs:49, 154) leaves video.h264 empty, so count_frames returns None ('the recording's video could not be read', recorder.rs:540-541) or 0 frames ('The recording is empty.', recorder.rs:543-545); a meta.json that does not parse is 'left alone' forever; the room shortage of VP-13 recurs every time. None of these folders (meta.json, tracks, a leftover mix.pcm) is ever removed. Each attempt also creates the game's Recordings folder through destination() before finalize (state.rs:1121, 1243-1245) and leaves it empty on failure. VP-13 covers the room guard underestimating; this finding covers recovery's error handling.
scenario: A recording crashes in a way recovery cannot finish (an empty or unreadable stream, or not enough room). Every later start spends seconds to minutes of disk and CPU on the same failing recovery. The user is never told that a recording exists, that it could not be finished, or why; only the log says so. The .recording folder (Windows does not hide dot-folders) stays in the clip folder indefinitely.
fix: Tell the user once about a failed recovery, naming the recording and the reason (for example 'needs X GB free'). Store an attempt count and the last error in meta.json and back off. Offer to delete, or delete after confirmation, folders that can never succeed (no frames, unreadable video or description). Delete mix.pcm when an attempt fails, and create the destination folder only after finalize succeeds (or prune it on failure).

title: When every recovery fails after encoding began, the closing progress event is never sent and the Record button stays disabled showing 'Saving recording… N %'
claim: lib.rs:280-282 reads `if !clips.is_empty() { recording_progress(&app, 1.0); }`, so the closing 1 goes out only when at least one recovery succeeded. finalize emits on_progress(0.1) (recorder.rs:592), and ffmpeg's out_time progress follows (muxer.rs:449-455), before encode can still fail: an ffmpeg error such as disk full while writing the MP4, 'cannot be read back', or replace_file. The store clears the bar only on share >= 1 (store.ts:289). Dashboard sets `saving = recordingSaving || recordingProgress !== null` (Dashboard.tsx:76), disables the Record button with `disabled={saving}` (line 122), and labels it 'Saving recording… N %' (lines 124-125); that label takes precedence over the Stop label even while a later recording runs. NavBar shows SavingBadge (lines 84-86). The stop path always emits 1.0 (lib.rs:241), and ipc.ts:222 documents '1 means done, either way'. The recovery path breaks that contract.
scenario: A crashed 2-hour recording whose MP4 does not fit (the VP-13 chain: mix.pcm fits, but writing the MP4 hits disk full). ffmpeg reports progress up to about 80 % and then fails, and give_up deletes the .part.mp4. The window keeps showing 'Saving recording… 80 %' with the Record button disabled and a saving badge in the nav bar. It clears only after the user starts and stops a recording by hotkey or tray. Because the leftover is retried at every start, this comes back at every launch.
fix: After recover_recordings returns, emit recording_progress(1.0) whenever any progress was emitted (or simply always), as stop_recording_and_notify does.

title: Numpad digit hotkeys depend on NumLock, and Shift+Numpad cannot be bound (likely recorded as the bare digit)
claim: supported() accepts Numpad0-9 and NumpadDecimal by event.code (line 91), and event.code is the same whether NumLock is on or off. key_to_vk registers VK_NUMPAD0-9 and VK_DECIMAL (mod.rs:295-306). Windows produces those VKs only with NumLock on. With NumLock off, the same keys produce VK_INSERT/END/DOWN/NEXT/LEFT/CLEAR/RIGHT/HOME/UP/PRIOR and VK_DELETE. With NumLock on, Shift plus a numpad digit makes Windows inject a Shift release and send the navigation VK instead, so MOD_SHIFT+VK_NUMPADn never matches. The webview then likely sees the digit's keydown with shiftKey false, so the recorder stores a bare "NumpadN".
scenario: (a) With NumLock off, a user records Num 1. It is saved without error and shown as 'Num 1', but pressing the key produces VK_END and the hotkey never fires until NumLock is turned on. (b) With NumLock on, a user tries Shift+Num 1 so that typing '1' stays free. The recorder most likely stores bare "Numpad1", and from then on every 1 typed on the numpad fires the action and is swallowed.
fix: Accept numpad digits only when event.getModifierState("NumLock") is true, or map by event.keyCode as proposed in the layout finding. Reject Shift+numpad-digit combinations and explain that Windows cannot register them.

title: Ctrl+ScrollLock, Ctrl+NumLock and Ctrl+Pause register virtual keys Windows never produces for those combinations
claim: The recorder accepts ScrollLock, NumLock and Pause with modifiers, and HARMLESS presents them as the quiet keys. Windows keyboard layouts treat NumLock and ScrollLock as multi-VK keys: with Ctrl held, NumLock produces VK_PAUSE and ScrollLock produces VK_CANCEL. Ctrl+Pause sends the Break scan code, which produces VK_CANCEL. global-hotkey registers MOD_CONTROL together with VK_NUMLOCK, VK_SCROLL or VK_PAUSE (mod.rs:294, 312, 322), which none of these key presses ever delivers.
scenario: A user binds Save clip to Ctrl+ScrollLock or Ctrl+NumLock, which is recorded by its physical code. The binding saves without error and never fires. If Ctrl+Pause gets recorded, it does not fire on Ctrl+Pause either; it fires on Ctrl+NumLock instead.
fix: In the recorder, reject Ctrl combined with Pause, ScrollLock or NumLock and show a short reason, or record these keys by event.keyCode (VK) so the stored binding matches what Windows delivers.

title: Recovery's `live` check only excludes a registered recorder, so a recording that is being stopped can be finalized twice at once
claim: recover_recordings skips only the folder of `self.recorder` (state.rs:1150-1155) and takes no lifecycle lock. stop_recording removes the recorder from `self.recorder` in close_recording (state.rs:1059), then runs finish_recording and finalize outside the lock (state.rs:1097). That takes tens of seconds to minutes, and all the while .recording/<id>/meta.json, now with frames set, is still there. Recovery runs once, when tools::setup reaches Ready (tools.rs:156-158). That can happen at any moment after a download or a Retry, and recording is allowed during the download when ffmpeg is on PATH (state.rs:978, `!is_ready() && !available()`). If Ready lands during a stop, leftovers() returns the folder being finalized and a second finalize starts on it. The matching start window (folder created at recorder.rs:139-144, recorder registered at state.rs:1000) is harmless in practice: video.h264 is still empty there, count_frames fails, and the folder is left alone.
scenario: First run, or the first run after an ffmpeg VERSION bump: the ffmpeg download is in progress and the user, who has ffmpeg on PATH, records and stops. While the stop's ffmpeg encodes, the download finishes and recovery starts on the same folder. Both runs align the tracks. The second sum_tracks re-creates mix.pcm with File::create, truncating it while the first ffmpeg reads it, so the first file's main mix can come out short. Both ffmpegs write the same stems::dir(id) tracks, and the first to finish deletes the work folder under the other. The result is two MP4s with different timestamped names and the same clip id. INSERT OR REPLACE keeps one row, the other file is orphaned, and the user gets both 'Recording saved' and 'A recording from last time was finished'.
fix: Keep the set of work folders being finished in AppState: insert in close_recording, remove after finish_recording. recover_recordings should skip those folders, or should take its leftovers snapshot under `lifecycle` and claim each folder (for example with a lock file) before finalizing.

title: A kill between the MP4 rename and the work-folder deletion makes the next start write a second full copy of the recording
claim: finalize is not idempotent. After muxer::encode renames the finished file into place (muxer.rs:375), it still writes the stem index and runs a second ffmpeg for the thumbnail (muxer.rs:379-387). Only then does finalize delete the work folder (recorder.rs:604). A kill in that window leaves both the finished MP4 and .recording/<id>/meta.json. The next start finalizes the folder again. finish_recording names the output with the current time (destination() uses jiff::Zoned::now(), state.rs:1226-1231), so it writes a second complete copy beside the first instead of over it. Only the second copy gets a library row. The first, the same recording at gigabytes in size, is never indexed and never removed by deleting the clip. Secondary path: if remove_dir_all fails with meta.json still present (it only logs a warning, recorder.rs:604-606), the clip has already been indexed, so the next start re-finalizes it and INSERT OR REPLACE (clips.rs:100) resets the row's title, description, favorite and edit.
scenario: The user stops a recording, or recovery is running, and the PC loses power or the user quits during the final thumbnail step at 'Saving recording… 99 %'. On the next start the user sees 'A recording from last time was finished' and the gallery shows one recording. The Recordings folder, however, holds two identical hour-long files with different timestamps, and the extra one uses as much space as the recording while staying invisible to the app.
fix: Make the output name deterministic for a work folder: derive it from meta.id or created_at, or save the chosen output path in meta.json before encoding. On recovery, if that output already exists and probes to the expected length, skip the encode and just index it. Use deleting meta.json, or renaming the folder, as the explicit commit point.

title: A crashed recording is recovered with only the game and friends from its start, and is named after the time of recovery
claim: meta.json gets its game and friends when the recording starts (state.rs:1029-1045, game_for(ZERO)). Only Recorder::finish updates the game (recorder.rs:343-351). Nothing rewrites meta.json when a game is detected during the recording, even though track_game updates buffering_game then (state.rs:681-683) and the code says a game detected half way should still claim the recording (recorder.rs:333-335). After a crash finish never ran, so the recovered clip carries the start-time game, or none. lib.rs:291 deliberately adds no current friends. destination() names the file with the recovery time, not meta.created_at. created_at, tags from meta.friends, and the current clip folder are otherwise used correctly.
scenario: The user starts recording on the desktop, launches Valorant, plays for two hours, and then the game takes the PC down. On the next start the recording lands in <clip folder>/Recordings/rec_<recovery date>.mp4 with no game, no game folder and no friend tags. A clean stop would have filed it as Valorant/Recordings/Valorant_rec_<time>.mp4 with the friend tags. A recording from Friday that is recovered on Monday carries Monday's date in its file name.
fix: Rewrite meta.json (game and friends) when the held game changes while recording, and name a recovered file from meta.created_at.
